help.intro: The closing conversation of this module, in your own AI assistant with voice on: things you did recently — your weekend, a trip, a meal — and who you did them with or for. Copy the exercise in, say 'Los geht's', answer in full sentences; the score and corrections arrive at the end. The tutor listens for the Perfekt with the right helper and the participle at the end, the dative for the receiver (Ich habe meiner Mutter geholfen; mit meinem Bruder), and time expressions that order the story (gestern, letzte Woche, zuerst, danach). Tell it like a story, one event after another.
help.tips[0].title: Order the story with time words
help.tips[0].text: Letztes Wochenende … Zuerst … Dann … Danach … Am Abend … Each one starts a sentence and the verb follows it.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Last Saturday I went to Bonn with my sister. First we …
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In the evening we ate together, and after that I went home.
help.tips[0].check.why: Zuerst takes position 1, so the verb (sind) follows it straight away, then the subject.
help.tips[0].visual.marks[1].label: then
help.tips[0].visual.marks[2].label: after that
help.tips[0].visual.marks[3].label: in the end
help.tips[1].title: With whom, for whom: dative
help.tips[1].text: mit meinem Freund, bei meinen Eltern, Ich habe meiner Mutter geholfen, Ich habe ihm ein Geschenk gegeben. Say the dative ending — it is what is scored.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: I cooked with my brother and helped my grandma.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Last week I helped my parents move house.
help.tips[1].check.q: Am Samstag war ich mit ____ Freundin im Kino.
help.tips[1].check.why: mit always takes the dative, and Freundin is feminine: mit meiner Freundin.
help.tips[2].text: The participle is the last word — don't trail off before it. 'Ich habe …' with no participle is not a sentence.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I watched a film — the last word makes it true.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: On Sunday I slept in and then visited my grandma.
help.tips[2].check.why: With habe, the sentence needs its participle at the very end: besucht. Without it, the sentence isn't finished.
help.remember[0]: Story words first, helper second, participle last.
help.remember[1]: mit + dem/der/meinem: the person you did it with is dative.
help.exam: Talking about past events and making plans together are both part of the A2 speaking exam — and of every catch-up with a friend.
help.hook: Tell a friend about your weekend: what happened first, who you were with, and every sentence finished with its last word.
speaking.topic: Things I did recently: my weekend, a trip, a meal, and who I did it with or for.
speaking.practisePoints[0]: Perfekt with haben and sein, participle at the end
speaking.practisePoints[1]: Dative for the receiver: Ich habe meiner Mutter geholfen.
speaking.practisePoints[2]: Time expressions in the past: gestern, letzte Woche, danach
speaking.scoringCriteria[3]: the dative after mit/bei and for the receiver
speaking.material:
Story beats, in order:
1. Last weekend (or a recent trip): where I went and with whom.
2. How I got there and what we did first.
3. What we ate, what I bought, and for whom.
4. One thing that went wrong or surprised me.
5. How it ended and how it was.
Follow-up questions at the end: who I did something for or gave something to (Wem hast du geholfen? Wem hast du etwas gekauft?), and what happened after that.
speaking.scoringNote: Count each beat I tell as one answer, and score the beat as a whole.
